d: An enlarged thyroid follicular cell whose cytoplasm is packed with mitochondria, so it stains pink and granular (oncocytic change); beside lymphoid follicles it marks Hashimoto thyroiditis.

Nonpitting swelling of the skin and soft tissues in severe hypothyroidism, caused by glycosaminoglycans that accumulate in the dermis and bind water; it produces a puffy face, thick tongue and hoarse voice.

The shutdown of organification by thyroid peroxidase when the gland receives a large iodide load, as from amiodarone or iodinated contrast; normal glands escape within days, damaged glands may stay hypothyroid.
A small, round, concentrically laminated calcification that forms around dead tumor cells; in the thyroid it points to papillary carcinoma.

The vagus branch that loops under the aortic arch on the left and the subclavian artery on the right, climbs in the tracheoesophageal groove and supplies every intrinsic laryngeal muscle except the cricothyroid; injury causes hoarseness.
